title: Priority-aware early-exit trace sampler to reduce hot-path overhead
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: The current tracing hot-path performs too many allocations and metadata enrichments before a sampling decision, causing measurable CPU and latency overhead on high-QPS services. Tail-capture heuristics and reservoir sampling are effective but expensive when applied universally. Goal: introduce a priority-aware early-exit trace sampler that makes a minimal, deterministic decision on the request hot-path using a tiny prefilter (header + route + error-indicator), and defers heavyweight work (span encoding, tag enrichment, reservoir bookkeeping) to asynchronous background workers for traces that are selected or require tail capture. The sampler should: (1) preserve or improve tail/error capture for high-severity requests, (2) reduce hot-path allocations and CPU on tracer clients by at least 15-20% for 99th-percentile hosts, (3) integrate with existing SDK flags and distributed context, and (4) be safe to roll out incrementally per-service or per-route.
acceptance_criteria: Hot-path allocation reduction: >=15% reduction in allocations measured by jemalloc/prof for tracer ingress path on representative 1M RPS test harness
CPU reduction: >=10% p99 CPU improvement for tracer processes under realistic workloads
Preserve tail/error capture: for synthetic error injections, >=95% of error traces that meet existing tail rules must still be captured
Canary rollout without instrumentation drift: sampling decision bit is compatible with downstream agents and bridges (no loss of existing spans)
Feature flag gated and rollbackable; metrics emitted for sampled, early-exit-skipped, deferred, and enriched counts
design_summary: We will implement a tiny prefilter-based sampler in the tracer hot-path that reads three low-cost signals: route fingerprint (hash of route id), customer tier (as a 2-bit priority tag), and an error-indicator bit set by instrumented HTTP/gRPC adapters. The sampler computes a single uint32 heuristic and applies a priority budget table to decide: (A) drop early (no allocation), (B) mark-as-deferred (record minimal header and enqueue for async reservoir consideration), or (C) accept immediately. Decisions are written as a single byte in the request context (early_exit_decision) to avoid additional allocations. The background worker maintains per-route, per-priority reservoirs and performs enriching (resolve user id, kv cache snapshot, span encoding) off the hot path. We will emit metrics: sampler.early_exit.count, sampler.deferred.count, sampler.accepted.count, sampler.reservoir.evictions, sampler.hotpath.alloc_bytes. Compatibility: SDKs will treat the decision byte as advisory; legacy collectors ignore it. The component uses atomic counters and a small lock-free ring buffer for enqueue; the ring buffer size is tunable per service via config. Backpressure logic: when enqueue buffer is near-full, downgrade deferred->drop for low-priority traffic and emit backpressure metric.
implementation_plan: Spike: 2025-02-13 - microbench prototype in tracer sidecar (branch: feat/early-exit-sampler-spike)
Library change: implement sampler C API that returns a byte decision; ensure zero allocations in fast-path (PR: github.com/redwood/tracer/pull/12345)
Background worker: implement reservoir manager and async enrichment pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood/observability/pull/6789)
Integration: wire decision bit through ingest proxy and collector (PR: github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/54321)
SDK updates: add optional opt-in to emit early-exit context for older SDKs (PR: github.com/redwood/sdk/pull/9876)
Testing: unit, load, chaos -> merge gate
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off by default. 2) Shadow mode for 2 services (5k RPS) for 48h, compare metrics. 3) Canary: enable for non-critical routes at 10% traffic for 24h. 4) Expand to 50% for 72h. 5) Global by route groups with 7d observation. Rollback criteria: >5% increase in end-to-end p99 latency, >2x increase in span loss for errors, or unexplained increase in tracer CPU beyond expected savings.
tests: Unit tests for decision logic and ring buffer edge cases
Microbench: show zero-alloc fast-path using go test/bench and async mock
Load test: 1M RPS harness with mixed priority traffic to validate allocation and CPU improvements
Chaos: simulate long background worker GC pauses and verify backpressure and downgrade behavior
E2E regression: replay historical production traces to ensure tail capture parity
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Spike completed. Prototype shows 18% allocation reduction on tracer ingress in synthetic benchmark.
2025-02-18: Early API landed in tracer library branch feat/early-exit-sampler. Hot-path validated for zero-alloc path in CI microbench.
2025-02-20: Background reservoir initial implementation completed; integration tests failing intermittently with KV cache race during enrichment (investigating).
2025-02-25: Discovered race caused by double-free of temporary metadata in rare fast-path->deferred transition. Patch proposed in PR #6792.
2025-02-28: Patch merged for race; integration tests now stable locally. Preparing shadow rollout for two low-risk services next week.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect early-drop could lose critical error traces -> Mitigation: conservative default budgets, shadow mode, and explicit error-indicator overrides that always accept

Risk: Background worker backlog under sustained burst -> Mitigation: backpressure metrics and automatic downgrade for low-priority traffic; operational runbook to increase buffer size or scale worker pool
Risk: SDK incompatibility -> Mitigation: decision is advisory and collectors ignore unknown bytes; we ship SDK opt-ins first
Risk: Observability blind spots during rollout -> Mitigation: tight dashboarding for span-loss, error capture rate, and sampling distribution; temporary retention of raw sampling telemetry for 7d
estimated_savings: ~15-20% tracer CPU p99 improvement and approx 10-15% downstream storage/write cost reduction for sampled traces on high-QPS services
